Slovenian professional [[basketball]] player who plays for [[KK Split|Split]] of the [[Premijer liga (Croatian basketball)|Croatian League]] and [[ABA League]]. He also represents the [[Slovenia national basketball team|Slovenian national basketball team]] internationally. Standing at {{height|m=1.96}}, he plays the [[shooting guard]] and [[small forward]] positions. He is the younger brother of [[Goran Dragić]]. ==Professional career== ===Early years=== In 2004, Dragić joined [[KD Ilirija|Ilirija]] of the Slovenian 1B league for the 2004–05 season. A year afterwards, he joined Janče STZ of the Slovenian D2 league for the 2005–06 season. During 2006, he signed with [[KD Slovan|Geoplin Slovan]] of the [[Premier A Slovenian Basketball League|Slovenian League]] where he went on to play four seasons for them. In 2010, he signed with [[BC Krka|Krka]] where he went on to play two seasons for them. === Málaga (2012–2014) === In July 2012, Dragić joined the [[Houston Rockets]] for the 2012 [[NBA Summer League]].{{cite news|title=Zoran Dragic will play the NBA Summer League with the Rockets|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/92117/zoran-dragic-will-play-the-nba-summer-league-with-the-rockets.html|date=May 30, 2012|access-date=September 30, 2014|work=Sportando.com}} On August 20, 2012, he signed a two-year deal with [[Baloncesto Málaga|Unicaja Málaga]] of the [[Liga ACB]].{{cite news|title=Unicaja Malaga signs Zoran Dragic to a two-year deal|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/spain/94658/unicaja-malaga-signs-zoran-dragic-to-a-two-year-deal.html|access-date=14 August 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=20 August 2015}} On July 8, 2014, he signed a two-year contract extension with Unicaja Málaga.{{cite news|title=Unicaja extends with Dragic for two more years|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/138537|access-date=July 8, 2014|work=Euroleague.net|date=July 8, 2014}} However, after agreeing to sign with the [[Phoenix Suns]], Dragić and Málaga agreed to part ways on September 26, 2014.{{cite news|title=Dragic se marcha a la NBA|url=http://www.unicajabaloncesto.com/noticia-9101-dragic-marcha-nba.html|date=September 26, 2014|access-date=September 29, 2014|work=unicajabaloncesto.com|language=es}} === Phoenix Suns (2014–2015) === On September 29, 2014, Dragić signed a two-year deal with the Phoenix Suns.{{cite news|title=Suns Sign Zoran Dragic|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-zoran-dragic|date=September 29, 2014|access-date=September 30, 2014|work=NBA.com}}{{cite news|last1=Stein|first1=Marc|title=Zoran Dragic, Suns reach deal|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/11588330/zoran-dragic-phoenix-suns-agree-two-year-deal|date=September 25, 2014|access-date=September 30, 2014|work=ESPN.com}} He went on to make his NBA debut on November 15, 2014, against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. He and Goran, alongside teammates [[Markieff Morris|Markieff]] and [[Marcus Morris (basketball)|Marcus Morris]], all briefly played together for the Suns during the fourth quarter of their 112–96 victory over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] on January 2, 2015. It marked the first time in the NBA's history that two different pairs of brothers played together for the same team at the same time. In what was just his third game of the season, he also recorded his first NBA stats with 3 points, 1 rebound, and 1 assist.[http://www.nba.com/games/20150102/PHIPHX/gameinfo.html Green helps Suns pull Pelicans]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-acquire-goran-dragic-and-zoran-dragic|title=HEAT Acquire Goran Dragic and Zoran Dragic|date=February 19, February 20, 2018, when he suffered a torn [[anterior cruciate ligament]]. Dragić nursed and recovered from his injury and returned in January 2019. He signed with Serie A club [[Pallacanestro Trieste|Alma Trieste]] on January 8, 2019, until the end of the 2018–2019 season. On August 6, 2019, he signed with [[ratiopharm Ulm]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL).{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/zoran-dragic-completes-ulm-roster-for-next-season/|title=Zoran Dragic completes Ulm roster for next season|date=August 6, 2019|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=September 19, 2019|last1=Carchia|first1=Emiliano|archive-date=August 6, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190806173732/https://sportando.basketball/en/zoran-dragic-completes-ulm-roster-for-next-season/|url-status=dead}} On January 30, 2020, Dragić officially signed with [[Liga ACB]] club [[Saski Baskonia|Baskonia]] for the rest of the season,{{Cite web|url=https://www.baskonia.com/zoran-dragic-experiencia-para-el-perimetro-azulgrana|title=Zoran Dragic, experiencia para el perímetro azulgrana|date=January 30, 2020|website=baskonia.com|language=ES|access-date=January 31, 2020}} making his return to the [[EuroLeague]]. Dragić|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Slovenia/news/957214/Split-lands-Zoran-Dragic|publisher=[[Eurobasket.com]]|access-date=September 21, 2025|date=September 20, 2025}} ==National team career== Dragić started playing for the Slovenian national junior team in the [[2007 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]]. He also participated in the [[2009 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]], during which he would be the tournament's 4th best scorer, throughout the entire competition. In 2011, Dragić participated with the Slovenian senior squad, alongside his brother, [[Goran Dragić|Goran]], during the [[EuroBasket 2011]] tournament. After the success he had in 2011, he also played for Slovenia in the [[EuroBasket 2013]] tournament, and helped the team finish with a better place in the final standings than the previous tournament. He went on to play for Slovenia in the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]], where his performance became a leading catalyst for his eventual signing with the [[Phoenix Suns]] later that year.[http://www.nba.com/suns/news/how-zoran-dragic-became-phoenix-sun How Zoran Became a Phoenix Sun] He represented Slovenia at the [[EuroBasket 2015]], where they were eliminated by [[Latvia
